summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of chronic abdominal pain, gastroparesis, anxiety, depression, and PTSD was admitted for an acute flare of abdominal pain consistent with prior episodes. She presented with epigastric pain, nausea, and vomiting, and was managed with an established inpatient protocol including IV fluids, pain control, and gradual dietary advancement. Labs showed mild, stable lipase elevation without evidence of acute pancreatitis. She improved over the course of the admission, tolerating soft foods and reporting decreased pain. No new complications arose. She was discharged home in stable condition with referrals to a new GI specialist and pain management, and a plan to continue home medications including erythromycin, metoclopramide, and hydrocodone as needed.
